_comment: THE BATTERIES CANDIDATE LIST, machine-readable so the gap can be REPORTED rather
than narrated. sources/report_candidate_gaps.py reads it and prints what is still
missing on every build.
WHY IT EXISTS. The perimeter admits a site only when the company has confirmed it
and a citable source identifies the works. Both take research, and a dataset in
build-up therefore has two populations: rows that are on file, and candidates that
are not yet. Held only in prose, the second population is a paragraph somebody has
to remember to update. Held here, it is a number the build prints.
A CANDIDATE LEAVES BY BECOMING A ROW. `id` matches the project id it will take in
data/transition/projects.json, and the report treats a candidate whose id is
already a project as landed. Nothing is deleted when that happens: the entry stays
as the record of what was needed, and the report stops asking for it.
`company_source` is a URL or null. `coordinate_source` is one of the values in
sector_map.LOCATION_SOURCE_TYPES or null. Null means outstanding, and outstanding
is the thing this file is for.
Refused candidates are NOT here. This file is the admitted set; what the perimeter
refuses, and why, is in sources/batteries_docket.md, which is the reviewed record.
`company_source_blocked` is the third state. The right document has been found and
named, and the fetcher cannot read it -- a publisher that answers 403 to a datacentre
IP, or a host whose certificate does not match. It is not a missing source and it is
not a usable one: somebody with a browser can close it in a minute, and until they do
the row cannot carry a verbatim quote nobody has read.

candidates.coordinate_ref: permit 21/01764/HE4, varied by 23/01542/VA4 (Sunderland City Council). Site address on the register: '1 International Drive, Sunderland SR5 3FH', tied to AESC Plant 2 through discharge-of-condition 24/00782/DIS, which names 23/01542/VA4 in its description.

candidates.note: Status and staleness both turn on the June 2026 update: the cornerstone was laid in July 2024, but as of June 2026 only ground preparation is done and AESC's roadmap puts first cells at December 2028. When the row lands it is construction — ground works have begun — with a note that four and a half years separate the cornerstone from the first cell. Not stale by the twelve-month test: the newest source is three months old.
candidates.company_source_blocked: https://www.aesc-group.com/newsInfo?id=<slug> — 'AESC Spain celebrates the laying of the first stone of the battery gigafactory in Navalmoral de la Mata (Cáceres)'. The live URL form is confirmed by the two pages already retrieved; the slug itself is not, so it is not guessed here.

supporting_sources.note: State primary for the cornerstone, located this pass and replacing nothing — it stands beside La Moncloa's rather than instead of it.
Cornerstone laid 8 July 2024, nearly €1 billion in the first phase.

Environmental authorisation put to public consultation. The four-phase build to 2028 and the 108-hectare plot in the Industrial Development Park of Northern Extremadura come from this line of documents; a capacity of 94.24 GWh at the end of phase four is stated in them and has not been read against an AESC figure.

supporting_sources.publisher: elEconomista, relaying the Junta de Extremadura
supporting_sources.note: RELAY, KEPT AS A LOCATOR. No Junta or Assembly record of the June 2026 update was found — the Junta's newsroom carries the cornerstone and the 2025 Zama visit but nothing from June 2026, and the Assembly's session records did not surface one. The substitution note therefore stands: this is press relaying a state source, recorded as press.

Company source in hand (SK Innovation network page, '2900 Komárom, Klapka György út 39.'). COORDINATE EXHAUSTED: a bounding-box sweep of 400 features across Komárom and Komárno returns nothing for SK On or SK Battery Manufacturing, and the published address geocodes only to the street.

candidates.coordinate_ref: way/1263927003 Hungary Sunwoda Electronics Automotive Energy, landuse=construction
candidates.note: COORDINATE FOUND, SITE RULE STILL UNMET. The basemap names the works — 'Hungary Sunwoda Electronics Automotive Energy' at Nyíregyháza — but Sunwoda's own release of 10 August 2023 says only 'Hungary' and names no city, and the 2025 milestones page does not mention the country at all. Site confirmation is company-only, so a basemap feature naming the operator does not close it. Trade press and HIPA both say cells rather than packs; Sunwoda's own words are 'lithium-ion batteries and power battery systems', which does not settle the product rule either.

Company source found: EVE's own page of 29 September 2025 names Debrecen — 'The EVE Energy Hungarian factory, approved for construction this year, is expected to be completed and put into operation in 2026.' No company capacity figure; the 30 GWh is state and trade tier. COORDINATE NOT FOUND: a sweep of 117 features across Debrecen returns the CATL site and nothing in the northwest industrial zone.

candidates.coordinate_ref: way/1262719042 Construção da Unidade Industrial de Baterias de Lítio da CALB
candidates.note: Coordinate in hand. CALB's own groundbreaking release is the right document and en.calb-tech.com serves a certificate for cloudfront.net.

The right document is identified — FREYR's operations update of 29 November 2023, which is where the Giga Arctic suspension is stated. Business Wire answers 403 to this pipeline, and so does T1 Energy's own investor site. Worth noting against the wire ruling: PR Newswire is readable here and Business Wire is not, so which wire a company used decides whether the release can be quoted.

Company source in hand (elevenes.com), which confirms both the 8 GWh gigafactory and the separate 1 GWh mega-factory. COORDINATE EXHAUSTED: a bounding-box sweep of 400 features across Subotica returns no feature named or operated by ElevenEs. Not outstanding for want of looking.

Company source in hand (PR Newswire, 10 December 2020). The permit route WORKED and the fetch did not: application 21/00818/FULES names the parcel exactly, and both the committee report and the public-access portal refuse this pipeline — 403 and 'no longer available for viewing'. The coordinate is not absent, as I said last turn; it is behind a document a browser opens. What occupies the parcel now — a data centre — does not bear on where the project was sited.
